name: GALLEX
notes: GALLEX (1991-1997) and its successor GNO (1998-2003) are recorded as ONE experiment, with GNO as an alias; there is no separate GNO record.

No official GALLEX/GNO site was found (a dedicated official site does not appear to exist independently of the MPIK Heidelberg host institution, which was not consulted); all facts here rely on Wikipedia and INSPIRE.

physics_goals.quote: It was designed to detect solar neutrinos and prove theories related to the Sun's energy creation mechanism.
physics_goals.value: Detect low-energy (pp-chain) solar neutrinos via the radiochemical gallium-to-germanium reaction and measure the total solar neutrino capture rate

summary.plain: An experiment in an Italian mountain lab that used tonnes of liquid gallium to catch the Sun's lowest-energy neutrinos, the ones from its very first fusion step.
summary.technical: Radiochemical gallium solar-neutrino experiment at LNGS: 30.3 t gallium (as 101 t GaCl3-HCl solution), sensitive to pp-chain neutrinos via the 71Ga→71Ge reaction. Ran as GALLEX 1991-1997 (73.1 SNU capture rate) then as GNO 1998-2003 (62.9 SNU), led by the Max-Planck-Institut für Kernphysik, Heidelberg, with French, German, Italian, Israeli, Polish and American participation.
